_readme: Accepted HIGH/CRITICAL advisories for `npm run check:dependency-audit:mobile` (run from the repo root).
Same contract as the web /.audit-allowlist.json — see its _readme for the field shapes and the rules.
Separate from the web allowlist ON PURPOSE: the two trees share almost nothing, and an accept reasoned
about a server code path means nothing inside an Expo bundle. Never paste an id between the two files
without re-arguing the reason for THAT tree.
Note the mobile gate covers the WHOLE tree, not just runtime deps: `--omit=dev` is inert under
`--package-lock-only` (verified 2026-08-07 — identical reports with and without it). That is the honest
posture for this tree anyway, since mobile's only devDependency is @babel/core.
Empty is the healthy state — the two linkify-it advisories that were briefly accepted here are fixed
instead, by the `linkify-it: ^5.0.2` override in mobile/package.json. See CHANGELOG 479.
The image-size accepts below are NOT fixable as of 2026-08-17: the vulnerable range is <= 2.0.2 and
2.0.2 is the LATEST published version — no patched release exists to bump or override to (upstream's
last release is 2025-04-02; verified against the GitHub advisories and the npm registry). Re-check
`npm view image-size versions` at expiry; the moment a patched release lands, fix via override on
metro's `image-size` dep and delete both entries.

accepted.reason: Build-time only, first-party input only. image-size is reached solely via expo > @expo/metro > metro (Assets.js), which parses the dimensions of image assets checked into THIS repo during bundling/export — it is not in the shipped app bundle and never parses attacker-supplied images. The DoS (infinite loop on a crafted ICNS file) could only hang our own build, and only if a malicious ICNS were committed to the repo. No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 2.0.2 = every published release).

Same code path and posture as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr: metro's build-time asset dimension probe over repo-owned images; JXL/HEIF infinite-loop variant. Not runtime-reachable in the app; worst case is a hung CI build from a malicious committed image. No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 2.0.2 = every published release).
